# Google Cloud WAF — performance optimization

Curated by Skill Harbor — @google's official skill for the Performance Optimization pillar of the Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework: it makes the agent apply the four core principles to a workload — plan resource allocation (matching compute/storage/network to workload requirements), take advantage of elasticity (autoscaling, serverless, scale-to-zero), promote modular design (loosely coupled components that scale and optimize independently), and continuously monitor and improve (observability, tracing, profiling, KPIs feeding iterative enhancement). Includes workload assessment questions per principle, relevant Google Cloud products and features (Compute Engine MIGs, GKE, Cloud Run, Cloud CDN, Memorystore, Bigtable, Spanner, Cloud Trace, Cloud Profiler, Cloud Monitoring), and a validation checklist covering provisioning based on load testing, multi-layer caching, circuit breakers, auto-scaling rules, and idle-overhead reviews. Honest caveats: guidance and assessment only — it does not provision or change cloud resources itself; product recommendations follow Google Cloud docs and may drift; Apache-2.0 licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
